rules: When a hart is executing in privilege mode x, interrupts are globally enabled if x IE is 1.
When a hart is executing in privilege mode x, interrupts are globally disabled if x IE is 0.
When a hart is executing in privilege mode x, interrupts for lower-privilege modes w < x are always globally disabled regardless of the value of w IE.
When a hart is executing in privilege mode x, interrupts for higher-privilege modes y > x are always globally enabled regardless of the value of y IE.
When a trap is taken from privilege mode y into privilege mode x, x PIE is set to the value of x IE, x IE is set to 0, and x PP is set to y.
When an x RET instruction is executed and x PP holds the value y, x IE is set to x PIE, the privilege mode is changed to y, x PIE is set to 1, and x PP is set to the least-privileged supported mode.
When an x RET instruction is executed and the new privilege mode y is not M, MPRV is set to 0.
The x PP fields can only hold privilege modes up to privilege mode x.
If privilege mode x is not implemented, then x PP is read-only 0.
When the MDT bit is set to 1 by an explicit CSR write, the MIE bit is cleared to 0.
When an explicit CSR write attempts to set the MIE bit to 1, the MIE bit is set to 1 only if the MDT bit is currently 0 or, for RV64, if the MDT bit is being set to 0 by the same write.
When a trap is taken into M-mode, if the MDT bit is 0, the MDT bit is set to 1.
When MRET or SRET is executed in M-mode, the MDT bit is set to 0.
When MRET, SRET, or MNRET is executed and the new privilege mode is U, VS, or VU, sstatus.SDT is set to 0.
When the MNRET instruction is executed, if the new privilege mode is not M, the MDT bit is set to 0.
When MXLEN=32, the SXL and UXL fields do not exist, and SXLEN is 32 and UXLEN is 32.
When MXLEN=64 and S-mode is not supported, SXL is read-only zero.
When MXLEN=64 and U-mode is not supported, UXL is read-only zero.
When S-mode is implemented and MXLEN=64, the set of legal values for UXL excludes those that would cause UXLEN to be greater than SXLEN.
When MPRV is 0, explicit memory accesses behave as normal, using the translation and protection mechanisms of the current privilege mode.
When MPRV is 1, explicit load and store memory addresses are translated and protected as though the current privilege mode were set to MPP.
The MPRV bit does not affect instruction address-translation and protection.
When U-mode is not supported, the MPRV bit is read-only 0.
When an MRET or SRET instruction changes the privilege mode to a mode less privileged than M, MPRV is set to 0.
When MXR is 0, only loads from pages marked readable (R=1) succeed.
When MXR is 1, loads from pages marked readable (R=1) or executable (X=1) succeed.
The MXR bit has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.
When S-mode is not supported, the MXR bit is read-only 0.
When SUM is 0, S-mode memory accesses to pages that are accessible by U-mode (U=1) fault.
When SUM is 1, S-mode memory accesses to pages that are accessible by U-mode (U=1) are permitted.
The SUM bit has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.
The SUM bit is in effect when MPRV is 1 and MPP is S.
When S-mode is not supported or if satp.MODE is read-only 0, the SUM bit is read-only 0.
When mstatus.MPRV is 0 and MBE is 0, non-instruction-fetch memory accesses in M-mode are little-endian.
When mstatus.MPRV is 0 and MBE is 1, non-instruction-fetch memory accesses in M-mode are big-endian.
When S-mode is supported and SBE is 0, explicit load and store memory accesses in S-mode are little-endian.
When S-mode is supported and SBE is 1, explicit load and store memory accesses in S-mode are big-endian.
When U-mode is supported and UBE is 0, explicit load and store memory accesses in U-mode are little-endian.
When U-mode is supported and UBE is 1, explicit load and store memory accesses in U-mode are big-endian.
For implicit accesses to supervisor-level memory management data structures, endianness is always controlled by SBE.
If S-mode is supported, SBE may be a read-only copy of MBE.
If U-mode is supported, UBE may be a read-only copy of MBE or SBE.
When MBE, SBE, and UBE are all read-only 0, the implementation supports only little-endian memory accesses.
When MBE is read-only 1, SBE is read-only 1, and UBE is read-only 1, the implementation supports only big-endian memory accesses (aside from instruction fetches).
When TVM is 1, attempts to read or write the satp CSR or execute an SFENCE.VMA or SINVAL.VMA instruction while executing in S-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception.
When TVM is 0, attempts to read or write the satp CSR or execute an SFENCE.VMA or SINVAL.VMA instruction while executing in S-mode are permitted.
When S-mode is not supported, the TVM bit is read-only 0.

When TW is 1, if WFI is executed in a mode less privileged than M and does not complete within an implementation-specific, bounded time limit, the WFI instruction causes an illegal-instruction exception.
When there are no modes less privileged than M, the TW bit is read-only 0.

When S-mode is implemented, executing WFI in U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception regardless of the value of the TW bit, unless the instruction completes within an implementation-specific, bounded time limit.
When TSR is 1, attempts to execute SRET while executing in S-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception.
When TSR is 0, executing SRET in S-mode is permitted.
When S-mode is not supported, the TSR bit is read-only 0.
The SD bit is set to 1 if any of the FS, VS, or XS fields encode a Dirty state.
If FS, VS, and XS are all read-only zero, the SD bit is set to 0.
If the F extension is implemented, the FS field shall not be read-only zero.
If neither the F extension nor S-mode is implemented, the FS field is read-only zero.
If the v registers are implemented, the VS field shall not be read-only zero.
If neither the v registers nor S-mode is implemented, the VS field is read-only zero.
In harts without additional user-extensions requiring new state, the XS field is read-only zero.
When the FS field is Off, any instruction that attempts to read or write the corresponding state causes an illegal-instruction exception.
When the FS field is Initial and an instruction is executed that possibly modifies state, the FS field transitions to Dirty.
When the FS field is Clean and an instruction is executed that possibly modifies state, the FS field transitions to Dirty.
When the FS field is Dirty and an instruction is executed that possibly modifies state, the FS field remains Dirty.
When the FS field is Off and an instruction is executed to unconfigure unit, the FS field remains Off.
When the FS field is Off and an instruction is executed to disable unit, the FS field transitions to Off.
When the FS field is Off and an instruction is executed to enable unit, the FS field transitions to Initial.
When the VS field is Off, any instruction that attempts to read or write the corresponding state causes an illegal-instruction exception.
When the VS field is Initial and an instruction is executed that possibly modifies state, the VS field transitions to Dirty.
When the VS field is Clean and an instruction is executed that possibly modifies state, the VS field transitions to Dirty.
When the VS field is Dirty and an instruction is executed that possibly modifies state, the VS field remains Dirty.
When the VS field is Off and an instruction is executed to unconfigure unit, the VS field remains Off.
When the VS field is Off and an instruction is executed to disable unit, the VS field transitions to Off.
When the VS field is Off and an instruction is executed to enable unit, the VS field transitions to Initial.
When the XS field is Off, any instruction that attempts to read or write the corresponding state causes an illegal-instruction exception.
When the XS field is Initial and an instruction is executed that possibly modifies state, the XS field transitions to Dirty.
When the XS field is Clean and an instruction is executed that possibly modifies state, the XS field transitions to Dirty.
When the XS field is Dirty and an instruction is executed that possibly modifies state, the XS field remains Dirty.
When the XS field is Off and an instruction is executed to unconfigure unit, the XS field remains Off.
When the XS field is Off and an instruction is executed to disable unit, the XS field transitions to Off.
When the XS field is Off and an instruction is executed to enable unit, the XS field transitions to Initial.
